newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND SAYS HACHETTE COURT CALL ON RUCH UNFOUNDED.
newsitem.headline: POLAND SAYS HACHETTE COURT CALL ON RUCH UNFOUNDED.

text.p: The Polish treasury ministry sees as unfounded French Hachette's appeal to a Warsaw court to rule on whether its initial deal on buying press chain Ruch SA is legally binding, a ministry adviser said on Friday.
Earlier this week Hachette asked a Warsaw court to rule whether its initial deal on buying press chain Ruch SA, signed in December with the treasury ministry but later annulled, was legally binding.

"In view of the lack of foundations of the demands, a court case by Hachette can be treated as an expression of dissatisfaction by one who took part in negotiations," PAP news agency quoted Zbigniew Ostrowski as saying.
"As far as the (court) appeal is concerned, we'll represent our viewpoint in court," he added.

Hachette had said the consortium it led containing Polish firms wanted the court to order the ministry to meet its earlier pledge to sell it the newsstand chain which controls 65 percent of Poland's press distribution market.
In March, the treasury ministry abandoned the initial agreement to sell a 75 percent stake in Ruch to the Hachette-led consortium and invited new bids for the company.

The ministry said it had put aside the deal with Hachette, which offered to pay $83 million for the Ruch stake, increase its capital by $45 million and then invest another $155 million, because a more attractive offer emerged.
Hachette said the ministry had treated it unfairly because it invited new bids for Ruch after the French-led group had unveiled terms of its offer and refused to bid in the new tender.
The ministry has said it shortlisted two bidders in the next tender, one of which is a Polish group led by Universal and including private television Polsat SA and soft drink producer Multico SA.
The group earlier said it was ready to pay $80 million for a 40-percent stake in Ruch and pledged to invest a total of $200 million in the company.
